summary: Iteration 38 testing — Night Angels free PDF, Lead-magnet, Coloring Studio (Nano Banana), Body Room images, Whispers attribution + WhispersPortal, BookDetail cross-sell, all verified end-to-end against the live preview URL. Backend pytest suite (test_iteration38.py) = 20/20 pass. Frontend playwright smoke = all critical data-testids, links, iframes, copy buttons, and tracker network calls confirmed. PDF byte-verified (magic %PDF, 7,861,452 bytes, content-type application/pdf). Whispers tracker fires correctly on ?w= navigation (POSTs slug + landing_path).

minor.issue: All 8 files on disk are JPEG bytes (FFD8 magic) but server advertises Content-Type: image/png. Browsers tolerate this, but the mismatch is a real correctness issue — either re-encode the files to true PNG or change the Content-Type to image/jpeg.

Frontend mounts WhispersTracker once but two identical POSTs fire on a single ?w= navigation (likely React StrictMode double-invoke in dev). Server dedupes correctly so no functional impact, but worth guarding with a useRef to avoid the second call in production.

ui_bugs.issue: Title for one book is literally rendered as 'YOU DON'T HAVE TO DANCE TO ANOTHER'S TUNE\n' — the trailing \n is a literal escape sequence stored in the title field, not interpreted as a newline. Visible on /bookstore and on the Beyond-the-Matrix-I cross-sell card.

action_items: Decide whether body-room images should be true PNG (re-encode) or change Content-Type header to image/jpeg — current state is a header/payload mismatch.
Strip the trailing literal '\n' from the 'You Don't Have to Dance to Another's Tune' book title in the seed data / DB.

(Optional) Add a useRef-guarded one-shot in WhispersTracker so React StrictMode double-mount doesn't fire two POSTs in dev. Server dedupes, so production impact is zero — purely cosmetic in network tab.
critical_code_review_comments: Lead-magnet endpoint correctly returns BOTH read_url and download_url and honours the 24h dedupe window with status='already_sent' on the second send.

Free-book ACL is sound: /api/books/free/the-night-angels-embrace/download serves anonymously while /api/books/free/beyond-the-matrix-i/download blocks (returns 404 in current implementation rather than 403 — semantically OK, but spec said 403; consider making it explicit 403 to match documentation).
Coloring generate-daily endpoint is properly idempotent and ADMIN_TOKEN-gated (header X-Admin-Token works; 401 without token).
WhispersPortal renders all 6 required data-testids cleanly and the personal link string is exactly 'https://prulesoul.site/?w=anna' as specified.
BookDetail cross-sell correctly differentiates audience: kids book hides 'Visit the Cabinet' CTA, adult book shows it linking to /clarity-release.
server.py is now well past the 700-line guideline (carry-over from iter28/29) — splitting whispers + coloring + lead-magnet routers into their own modules is overdue.

success_rate.frontend: 100% on all iter38-relevant flows (PDF download link + iframe, cross-sell kids vs adult, coloring 3 pages + age filters present, WhispersPortal data-testids + 4 asset links + 5 copy buttons, WhispersTracker fires on ?w= navigation)

test_credentials: ADMIN_TOKEN read live from /app/backend/.env (5NebFHBpdy-...). No new credentials created. Lead-magnet tests use throwaway tester+<uuid>@example.com addresses.
seed_data_creation: None. Test slugs (test-w-<rand>) are scoped and dedupe-bound to the synthetic session.
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_iteration38.py owns the iter38 surface (Night Angels free PDF + lead-magnet + coloring + body-room + whispers track/summary). Run with `pytest backend/tests/test_iteration38.py -v`. The body-room image test deliberately accepts both PNG and JPEG magic because the on-disk files are JPEG-encoded despite the .png filename — this is documented as a minor backend issue, not a test bug. Lead-magnet test_send_returns_links uses a unique email per run to avoid the 24h dedupe window collapsing the test.
rca of the issue: Body-room PNG/JPEG mismatch RCA: the 8 files in /app/backend/storage/body_room/*.png are stored with .png extensions but contain JPEG byte streams (FFD8 FF E0). The FastAPI handler hard-codes media_type='image/png' based on extension. Mitigation: either (a) re-save originals via PIL `Image.open(...).save(..., format='PNG')` to align bytes with extension, or (b) inspect the magic bytes when serving and respond with the correct Content-Type. Option (a) is cheaper and one-time.
